thread:
John (ACME): hey team — started getting 429s on POST /v1/generate about 08:12 UTC. sudden spike, our app hit free plan burst cap. no auth errors, keys valid. can you confirm what's tripping?

Priya K (Support): sorry you're hitting this, john. can you paste the exact error body you see and the request-id header? also which org/account id?

John (ACME): error body: 
{
  "error": {
    "type": "rate_limited",
    "message": "request rate limit exceeded (burst_protection)"
  }
}
headers: x-request-id: abc123-req-778
org: acme-inc (free tier)
we can reproduce locally by hammering the endpoint with our background sync.

support-bot: Automated policy note: request abcd123 matched quota policy: free_plan::burst_protection -> short window limit applied. For immediate guidance see /docs/rate-limits.

Priya K (Support): thanks — looks like the burst_protection short-window was triggered (free tiers have conservative burst allowance). two paths: 1) temporary sales-assisted quota bump for a short window, or 2) short-term app-side mitigation (recommended) while you patch the job. do you need us to loop in sales for a temporary exception? :slightly_smiling_face:

John (ACME): we'd appreciate a short exception for 24h while we add jitter to the sync job. could you escalate to sales? this is production-impacting.

Sam R (Billing): pinging @Liam S from Sales. free plan exceptions are rare but we can do a timeboxed bump if risk is low. need: org id, burst window start/time, avg rps during spike, and an owner confirming rollback.

Liam S (Sales): on it. john, can you DM me the org id and a contact for a quick sign-off? also confirm desired increase: temporary +3x burst for 24h? we'll triage with infra.

John (ACME): DM sent. yes +3x for 24h. we will throttle fallback to single-worker if still hit.

Priya K (Support): while sales reviews, a few mitigations you can apply immediately: 
- add exponential backoff and jitter on 429s
- reduce concurrency for the background sync to 2 workers
- implement client-side token bucket to limit burst to ~10 req/s

Example repro (quick test to hit burst limiter):
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
    -H "X-Request-ID: test-burst-$i" \
    -d '{"model":"gpt-open-lite","input":"x"}' &
done
wait
```
Expected: first N requests succeed, then 429s with body above. If you can capture sampled x-request-ids we can map to infra logs.

John (ACME): repro confirmed, getting 200s then 429s after ~60 concurrent hits. attaching a short log snippet: 
```
2026-03-15T08:11:58Z request test-burst-12 200
2026-03-15T08:11:58Z request test-burst-13 200
2026-03-15T08:11:59Z request test-burst-64 429
2026-03-15T08:12:00Z request test-burst-65 429
```

Priya K (Support): perfect — send over a few failing x-request-ids (like test-burst-64) and we can correlate. also note: billing won't charge for a temporary sales exception, it's just capacity gating.

Liam S (Sales): quick update from infra — we can provide a 24h temporary increase of burst capacity for acme-inc while you deploy the fix. created ticket SLS-9876 and scheduled window starting 08:30 UTC. please keep the rollback plan ready.

John (ACME): that's great, thank you. we'll push a configuration change to add jitter + backoff in the next 20m. can you confirm we'll get a notice when the window starts/ends?

Liam S (Sales): yes — I'll add you to the ticket and you should get automated notifications. will also post here when change is applied.

support-bot: Change SLS-9876: temporary_burst_increase applied for org acme-inc. window: 2026-03-15T08:30Z -> 2026-03-16T08:30Z.

John (ACME): window started for us, tests show reduced 429s. patch deployed. really appreciate the quick help :raised_hands:

Priya K (Support): glad that helped. we'll keep the ticket open until end of window. if you see any lingering auth or quota anomalies share request-ids. closing from support side after window ends unless you ask otherwise.

John (ACME): will do. thanks everyone!
